candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record provides multiple clues pointing to volitional, goal-directed behavior with clear external incentives: selective acceptance of benzodiazepines/gabapentin while refusing other medications, purposeful movements to obtain lorazepam after seizures, and self-induced incontinence. These external incentives (obtaining controlled substances, avoiding homelessness/unemployment consequences, repeated ED visits) align with malingering rather than factitious disorder. Factitious disorder is a related but incompatible subtype because it excludes external motivators that are prominently present here.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Factitious disorder (imposed on self) vs. Malingering — both involve deliberate symptom feigning but differ critically in motivation: factitious disorder requires absence of external incentives (motivation is to assume sick role), whereas malingering requires identifiable external gain

case_quality_flags: Distinction between malingering and factitious disorder hinges on external vs. internal motivation — the record provides explicit behavioral evidence of external gain (controlled substance acquisition), supporting malingering over factitious disorder
